html:
The Cora, who call themselves Náayerite, are a Native American people of the Sierra del Nayar in the Mexican state of Nayarit. The map names them Xecora. They speak a Uto-Aztecan language close to that of their neighbours the Huichol.

They farmed maize in the steep mountain valleys and kept a strong religious centre on the Mesa del Nayar. Their rough country let them stay free long after the rest of western Mexico fell to Spain. Spanish armies failed to take the Sierra for almost two hundred years, and it was only conquered in 1722, among the last parts of New Spain to be subdued. Jesuit missionaries followed.

The Cora still live in the Sierra and keep their own festivals, among them a famous Holy Week that mixes Catholic and older rites. See also Náayerite on the modern map.
